Organising Committee

The team behind FLPT 2026.

Workshop Organisers

Francesco Quinzan University of Oxford

Senior Research Associate

Member of the Oxford Martin School, with an affiliated appointment at the University of Cambridge. His research lies at the intersection of AI safety, statistical learning, robustness, and alignment of foundation models. His work was recognised with fellowships and competitive grants from UKRI, COST, and other international programmes. He organised the 2025 ML for Drug Discovery Workshop and the 2025 LLM@Oxford Workshop.

Fanghui Liu University of Warwick

Assistant Professor

Faculty member affiliated with the University of Warwick and Shanghai Jiao Tong University. His research studies the foundations of modern machine learning from the perspective of learning efficiency, nonlinearity, and post-training. Recipient of the AAAI New Faculty Award and Rising Stars in AI recognition. Main organiser of the NeurIPS 2024 Fine-Tuning Workshop.

Azalia Mirhoseini Stanford University

Assistant Professor

Founder of Ricursive Intelligence. Her research focuses on scalable and self-improving AI systems, including foundational work on inference-time scaling of LLMs. Recognised with the Okawa Research Grant, the Google ML and Systems Junior Faculty Award, and MIT Technology Review’s 35 Under 35, with publications in venues including Nature.

Chengchun Shi London School of Economics and Political Science

Associate Professor

His research focuses on the statistical foundations of reinforcement learning, causal inference, and LLMs. Recipient of the Peter Gavin Hall IMS Early Career Prize, the IMS Tweedie Award, and the Royal Statistical Society Research Prize. Organiser of the 2026 Sanya Workshop on Causality and ML and the MLStat 2026 Conference.

Valentina Zangirolami University of Milano-Bicocca

Ph.D. Student

Her research studies reinforcement learning under partial observability and feedback-driven adaptation, with a focus on statistical inference and robustness in sequential learning problems, and applications to model fine-tuning under changing environments. Previously worked as a data scientist at Accenture.
